A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same V-Co study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reformatting and added experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet-256 generation results, controlled architectural and training ablations, and generated samples in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds computational-efficiency measurements, alternative-encoder ablations, and ImageNet-512 generation results.

M1.justification: The dual-stream architecture, structural masking for CFG, perceptual-drifting hybrid objective, and RMS calibration remain unchanged. Alternative encoders are tested within the existing framework; the PDFs do not establish a changed proposed procedure.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates ImageNet-256, while v2 additionally trains and evaluates generation at 512×512 resolution in Appendix B and Table 16. This extends resolution coverage within the same ImageNet class-conditional task.

E2.justification: Corresponding architecture, guidance, auxiliary-loss, and reference comparisons retain their comparator sets. The new efficiency and resolution comparisons reuse JiT variants already compared in v1; alternative encoders are components of V-Co ablations.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce ImageNet-512 evaluation at 200 and 600 epochs, alternative encoder configurations, and training-GFLOP and inference-throughput metrics. Table 6 specifies including DINOv2 in training compute and excluding it during inference. The retained experiments' documented training and sampling configurations are otherwise unchanged.

E4.justification: New Table 15 tests the hybrid loss and RMS scaling with MAE-L/16, SigLIP2-L/16, and CLIP-B/16, extending the encoder-dependence analysis. Table 6 adds computational-efficiency analysis. These are focused additions to the retained architecture, guidance, loss, gating, temperature, and DINOv2-size ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed variability, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars for the experimental results. The added experiments continue point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: v2 substantially expands reported evidence with compute/throughput results, alternative-encoder scores, ImageNet-512 results, and additional samples. Table 16 reports V-Co-B/16 ImageNet-512 FIDs of 2.93 and 2.42 at 200 and 600 epochs. In retained Table 5, its 600-epoch ImageNet-256 FID/IS changes from 2.33/250.1 to 2.35/261.1. The DINOv2-Base row at lambda_d=0.1 changes from unguided FID/IS 8.83/120.6 and guided 5.54/154.8 to 6.35/140.0 and 4.11/174.8, respectively, in v1 Table 13 versus v2 Table 14.

T1.justification: The co-denoising equations, hybrid-field construction, RMS scaling rule, and derived timestep transformation retain their mathematical substance. v2 condenses the SNR explanation and changes notation and equation grouping without adding a new theoretical result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the controlled-study contribution, the same recipe components, and the principal ImageNet performance claims. Grouping four ingredients into two themes in the abstract does not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that the recipe generalizes across visual encoders and higher resolution, and improves the quality–compute trade-off. Appendix B removes the explanation attributing DINOv2-size behavior to shared distillation. The substantive limitations concerning class conditioning, teacher dependence, and richer supervision remain.

D1.justification: New Appendix D states that complete training and inference code accompanies the supplementary material; actual availability is not established by the PDFs. Table 6 clarifies encoder cost accounting. Conversely, v2 removes the fourth-block REPA implementation detail and Table 3's individual best CFG values, without documenting changed settings.

R1.justification: v2 removes the original REPA paper by Yu et al., listed as reference 47 in v1. The encoder-size discussion also drops its iREPA/REPA comparisons and retains only RAE. The broader related-work framing and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the abstract and introduction, condenses the SNR explanation, adds a short reproducibility section, and updates affiliations and acknowledgments. The main section sequence and most explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with widespread resizing and relocation of figures and tables. Figure 4's panels are stacked, several captions are shortened, and Tables 6, 15, and 16 and Figure 9 are added. Existing sample grids in Figures 6–8 are retained.

improvement.justification: The alternative-encoder and higher-resolution tests strengthen support for generality, while Table 6 makes computational costs clearer. These gains outweigh limited reporting losses, but v2 removes some REPA/CFG details and introduces an unexplained discrepancy: Table 16 gives ImageNet-256 FID 2.70 for V-Co-B/16 at 200 epochs, whereas Table 5 retains 2.52. The net improvement is therefore modest.
